scenes.headline: How one model draws boxes, points and mattes
scenes.sub: A perception model built on Qwen3-VL
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Wick! This model answers a picture with boxes, points and masks. Here is how.

scenes.text: A language model writes boxes as coordinate tokens, and one special token hands each object to a small pixel decoder.
scenes.say: The model writes coordinates as tokens. A special object token then hands each object to a small decoder that draws the mask.

steps.say: The photo goes through a vision tower that turns patches into features.
The language model reads those features and the question.
It answers with text. For each object, four coordinate tokens and an object token.
The decoder takes that object token and its box, and reads the vision features.
Out comes a mask, or a full alpha matte for hair and fur.

scenes.label: new tokens: 1,001 coordinates and nine tags
scenes.say: The whole interface is one thousand and ten new tokens. A thousand and one coordinates, and nine tags, including the object token.

scenes.label: values more than the base model
scenes.note: an untied output head plus 744 new rows
scenes.say: The weights show where the size went: about three hundred ninety three million extra values, an output head no longer tied to the embeddings.

scenes.title: What a mask request really does
scenes.say: The released engine works in two passes.

items.say: First it generates the answer, boxes and object tokens.
A parser keeps the boxes that end in an object token.
Then it runs the whole model again on the finished answer, to read each object token.
Last, the decoder paints each instance on a canvas of one thousand twenty four pixels.

scenes.label: per mask instance, on the 1,024 pixel canvas
scenes.say: That decoder is small in values but not in work: about two hundred eighty eight billion operations per instance.

scenes.text: No SAM at inference, but SAM-made labels in training: the decoder is only as good as its teachers.
scenes.mark: only as good as its teachers
scenes.say: Remember this: no SAM at inference, but SAM made labels in training. The decoder is only as good as its teachers.

recap: One token hands objects to a 9.6M decoder.
scenes.say: Boxes are tokens. A small decoder draws the masks. And masks cost a second pass.
